commands.name: dataviz
commands.description: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. When the destination is a first-party document connector (host-designated, never self-described) that renders live charts, hand it the rows (inline, or as an uploaded data file the chart cites) rather than a rendered PNG/SVG — a picture of a chart loses hover, data inspection and per-value comments. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".

Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.

Don't invoke it on a diff that only touches tests, docs, or other code with no runtime surface to drive (a change to product source always has one) — there's nothing to observe.

Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply them to the working tree after the review. Pass --max-findings <n> to report up to n findings, or --max-findings all for every finding. The choice stays until you pass --max-findings default. For ultra on a GitHub.com PR target, --post asks to post the finished review’s findings to the PR as a single comment from the user’s GitHub account (not a review; the launch dialog still confirms in interactive sessions, while non-interactive mode posts on the flag alone) and --no-post hides that option.

# INDEX_RULES.md — Global Rules & Doc Routing

**Doc link:** <https://github.com/brando90/agents-config/blob/main/INDEX_RULES.md>

**TLDR:** Read this compact contract at task start, then read only the detailed rule sections whose triggers apply. All agents use the same policy; client-specific loading differs.

## How to load these rules

Refresh `~/agents-config` with `git -C ~/agents-config pull --ff-only` at each new non-trivial task and after an hour; preserve dirty/concurrent work and use the local copy if offline. Reread this index and relevant changed rules. When editing agents-config in an isolated checkout, use that checkout's index and detail files after refreshing the home checkout.

All Hard Rule **Details** links and matching Trigger Rule/Guideline links are mandatory routing: **before the action they govern, read that detail section and its applicable workflow**, including secret overrides, spending and review decisions. Do not read every topic file. Rule numbers are stable; paths below resolve beneath `~/agents-config/` (or the active agents-config checkout). If files are unavailable locally, fetch the same path under `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/brando90/agents-config/main/`. A Markdown link is a reading instruction, not proof the client loaded it. Never eagerly import this index or the detail collection into an entry file; read them as task files.

Hard rules govern conflicts with older wording in a triggered procedure. Explicit user instructions and platform/tool constraints retain their normal precedence. The SNAP pre-approval in Trigger Rule 51 is scoped to authorized work and existing budgets. Detail pages retain the procedures, examples and exceptions; the catalog is optional lookup.

## Hard Rules (every response, never skip)

1. **Protect secrets.** Never commit credentials; inspect the exact staged diff and filenames before committing or pushing. Do not print secret values. Stop on a suspected leak and rotate exposed credentials; references/env vars replace embedded secrets. [Details](rules/safety-and-models.md#hard-rule-1)

2. **Sync, then verify before pushing.** `git fetch` first; if upstream moved, rebase and re-test; never force-push a shared branch. Never fabricate unavailable source content; mark it unresolved. Inspect the diff and run the relevant deterministic checks. Report actual evidence and limitations, not an untested success claim. [Details](rules/maintenance.md#hard-rule-2)

3. **Quality assurance (QA) is opt-in.** Only a tier Brando explicitly requests or sets for this work in a runbook, `[qa]`/`[light-qa]`/`[mega-qa]` commit tag or environment flag starts a model reviewer. Hooks, project files and older “QA required” text are not opt-in. “Do QA”/“light QA” means one opposite-company round; apply findings and verify without automatic re-review. Mega QA follows Trigger Rule 10. Hooks cannot impose unsolicited QA; do not mention QA when unrequested. Benchmark-reference acceptance (43) remains separate. [Details](rules/safety-and-models.md#hard-rule-3)

4. **Response ending and titles.** Compact results: 1–2 sentences plus `.md`/`gdoc` links. End `**TLDR-end:** [proj: task]` with 1–2 sentences (`[proj]` without a task); never open `TLDR-start`. Emails/status reports also end `TLDR-end:` before any signature; include real decisions/deadlines only. Name and restate the core deliverable, not a micro-step (optional `›` suffix). Research updates open with a copy-ready status sentence; results also include a 1–2 sentence collaborator message in Brando’s voice. Match owned titles to verified summaries, identifier first. [Details](rules/responses.md#hard-rule-4)

5. **Snapshot.** In chat, immediately after the closing summary, show `**Snapshot:**` with the smallest real artifact sample (normally 5–15 lines, at most 25), or say why nothing tangible exists. [Details](rules/responses.md#hard-rule-5)

6. **Refresh configuration.** Follow the task-start/hourly refresh above, reread relevant changes, and preserve other owners’ work. Shared edits belong in both entry points. Review remains opt-in under Hard Rule 3. [Details](rules/maintenance.md#hard-rule-6)

7. **Keep clients current.** Use the installed package manager and the supported update hook; never assume npm. Do not install/use the deprecated Gemini CLI. [Details](rules/maintenance.md#hard-rule-7)

8. **Models, budgets and acceptance.** Masters: Codex `gpt-6-astra` / `ultra`; Claude `claude-fable-5-1` / `max`. Keep configured defaults; explicitly select proportionate execution workers (experiment selection: Guideline 19). Verify actual models/efforts and billing route (subscription or in-scope provider key). Never buy credits, enable new charges or weaken acceptance to recover. Required models/families and scientific pins remain binding. Before dispatch/review, read this detail and Rule 48. [Details](rules/safety-and-models.md#hard-rule-8)

9. **Model access: CLIs, subscriptions and provider keys are allowed.** Agents may wire Brando's existing provider keys into agent clients, write provider application programming interface (API) calls and run key-loading scripts without asking. Load keys at runtime, never print or commit them, keep each within its owner's scope and existing budgets, and cap and cost-estimate key-billed batch or unattended runs. [Details](rules/safety-and-models.md#hard-rule-9)

10. **Explain terminology.** Expand every acronym, metric symbol and project-specific term on first use in each response, chat included; use descriptive names, not opaque internal labels. For Brando, a code may lead if a short gloss follows on first use. [Details](rules/responses.md#hard-rule-10)

11. **Numbers with verdicts.** Compact entries link full statistics (Rule 4). Give measured values, scales, denominators/splits, threshold sources, missing measurements. Statistical headlines need 95% intervals (resampling unit, limits) and `x [lo, hi] p-val=Z` (named test/null or `p-val=n/a`). Report correlations individually; when interpreting score levels, add absolute agreement and mean bias (judge minus human, positive = lenient) with both means. Give repeated-score variability/counts. Existing data only; read the statistics workflow first. Research precision (10-24-2026): read settings, definitions, numbers from the repo, run records or paper; `unknown` only after a named-path search (in caption). VeriBench tables carry a Pi + best open-weight row. [Details](rules/responses.md#hard-rule-11)

| [56](rules/services.md#trigger-rule-56) | New day/planning/pasted task list → read weekly-notes source when available, compare latest section, disclose gaps; edit it only when Brando asks, additively. |
| [57](rules/workers.md#trigger-rule-57), [74](rules/workers.md#trigger-rule-74) | Would stall on scope, routing, approval or a click → decide (no-human route), record it; no self-made gates; to-dos only Brando's own. Grade next steps /10; do ≥9 now. |
| [58](rules/workers.md#trigger-rule-58) | Capacity/tool gap → checkpoint and continue through eligible existing accounts/agents; one failed route is not all accounts exhausted. |
| [59](rules/services.md#trigger-rule-59) | Mac freeze/Chrome zombie leak → load diagnosis playbook and repair the responsible parent, preserving tripwire. |
| [60](rules/writing.md#trigger-rule-60) | Technical explainer/teaching → use explainer style; paper prose uses its separate research style. |
| [61](rules/research.md#trigger-rule-61) | Solver/agent evaluation → freeze and finish full declared set within fixed budgets; retain every failed/missing cell and distinguish recovery. |
| [62](rules/services.md#trigger-rule-62) | Connector use, host setup, or unfamiliar/failing tool/service → read the connector cross-check and verified-host routes; investigate evidence, never fabricate missing content, recover and verify. |
| [63](rules/services.md#trigger-rule-63) | “Text me” → WhatsApp self-chat via quiet verified route; confirm sent state and surface human-only linking. |
| [64](rules/research.md#trigger-rule-64) | Explicit weekly update → newest-first project folder, complete post plus appendix/images; publish and return full post/path; keep sealed data sealed; sync knowledge under Rule 16; preserve his task-list text. |
| [65](rules/services.md#trigger-rule-65) | Open files for Brando in an editor → one call `cursor -n <project root> <files…>` (new window for that project); never `-r` or per-file open prompts. |
| [66](rules/services.md#trigger-rule-66) | Brando's AI meeting notes (Fathom link/ID, "get my notes") → verbatim transcript first, then summary and action items; script-written byte-exact copies with provenance in the named folder; never retype or reconstruct. |
| [67](rules/workers.md#trigger-rule-67) | Brief a worker, write a prompt or describe what an agent may do → default to allowed; state only binding limits, no precautionary bans or reassurance. |
| [68](rules/services.md#trigger-rule-68) | Create or copy a Google Doc/Sheet/Slides/Drive file → share "Anyone with the link" at creation: Viewer by default, Editor when readers fill it in; restricted only for secrets, sealed or private data. |
| [69](rules/workers.md#trigger-rule-69) | Dispatch or wait on a worker → watch for death too (`scripts/watch_worker.sh`: done, dead, credit/limit-blocked, idle, timeout); on failure recover at once on the next eligible account (Rule 58). |
| [70](rules/services.md#trigger-rule-70) | Launch or finish an experiment or long job (training/eval, cluster/background job, or >~15 min; never chat turns) → `[RUN START] <name>` then `[RUN DONE] <name>: <status>` email; recipient copies per Rule 26, deduplicate with Rule 14. |
| [71](rules/services.md#trigger-rule-71) | Session start, shared state, or need the assistant → `agent_sync.py check` the SYNC.md, name conflicts; read `[FROM-UB9]` in the repo's inbox issue (#68); ask with `[TO-UB9]` + email. |
| [72](rules/services.md#trigger-rule-72) | Launch/resume a Vals-paid run → one large experiment at a time across projects (`valk` gate); queue, estimate cost; only Brando overrides. |
| [75](rules/workers.md#trigger-rule-75) | Run pending, capped or failed on one cluster → try every reachable cluster yourself on empty GPUs, free hardware, no Duo; release idle. |
| [73](rules/workers.md#trigger-rule-73) | Desktop session pins → only active or awaiting-Brando sessions, dated title; unpin sessions when done (never Projects, Rule 86). |
| [76](rules/research.md#trigger-rule-76) | Design, launch or interpret an experiment, benchmark, agent eval, scorer or parser feeding a reported number, or a surprising number → load `workflows/ml-research-practice.md`: predict every metric (incl. literal compliance) before running, trace one item, controls, look at the data. |
| [77](rules/research.md#trigger-rule-77) | Build, select, validate or deploy an LLM judge/grader/reward model, or a claim it "agrees with humans" → load `workflows/llm-judge-recipe.md`: input audit, label-reproduction test, controls, test once, ICC. |
| [78](rules/hosts.md#trigger-rule-78) | Write/submit an `sbatch` script on any Slurm cluster → `--mail-type=END,FAIL` to brando.science only (Brando, 10-29-2026); `BEGIN` only if long/key; one mail per array. |
| [79](rules/responses.md#trigger-rule-79) | Sending/posting/saving anything a person reads (message, email, slide, Doc, README, PR) → spell-check it; Brando's surname is Miranda; check names against a source; quotes, identifiers and code keep their spelling. |
| [81](rules/maintenance.md#trigger-rule-81) | Verified work, any Brando repo → land on `origin/main` now; never park on a branch. |
| [80](rules/hosts.md#trigger-rule-80) | Launch/queue/size any GPU run, or free GPUs on mercury1/2 → use mercury as much as possible, whole node OK; empty GPUs only, never touch running jobs, shard big models over 4-5 A4000s, release when done. |
| [82](rules/research.md#trigger-rule-82) | Plan, run, score or report anything on public VeriBench → use the current release (`veribench@1.3`, 896 tasks, 10-28-2026); before each run `git ls-remote` veribench `main` and read its README release section; name the version beside every number. |
| [83](rules/research.md#trigger-rule-83) | Research/startup/eval with unknown need → ask if it should exist; run the quickest de-risking test locally, email results, write repo MD files; endpoints/logins in parallel; once it covers the main risk, push velocity. |
| [84](rules/research.md#trigger-rule-84) | Run/score/report vb-priv (or new VeriBench runs) → int_ref is the most important metric: run it once, save per-task results, derive int from it, lead updates with it. |
| [85](rules/writing.md#trigger-rule-85) | Write/edit/review ML research text (papers, reports, research Docs, updates) → load `skills/scientific-terminology`: one term per concept, reuse exactly, no stylistic synonyms. |
| [86](rules/workers.md#trigger-rule-86) | Claude app/claude.ai session start, Project change, new account sign-in, or Projects missing from the left → every Project of every account stays pinned in the sidebar; pin missing ones, run the session sync with `--all-accounts`, report counts; never wait to be asked. |

## Guidelines (best practices)

- [14](rules/maintenance.md#guideline-rule-14): Complete direct authorized requests; do not ask again for already-authorized actions.
- [15](rules/maintenance.md#guideline-rule-15): Read only task-relevant referenced docs.
- [16](rules/maintenance.md#guideline-rule-16): Keep index, README and paths accurate; mirror shared entry bodies; verify actual host instruction files and reload state.
- [17](rules/responses.md#guideline-rule-17): Use anchored paths in prose and commands.
- [18](rules/maintenance.md#guideline-rule-18): Use `ls -la` for configuration/credential directories.
- [19](rules/research.md#guideline-rule-19): Select experiment models/judges by capability, total cost and validation; preserve pins.
- [20](rules/responses.md#guideline-rule-20): Messages/drafts as Brando use his concise first-person voice; email includes required routing/signature.
- [21](rules/maintenance.md#guideline-rule-21): Check `~/keys/` for credentials, model-provider keys included, before asking; keep values transient.
- [22](rules/maintenance.md#guideline-rule-22): Let the Node version manager control its path; avoid hardcoded versioned PATH entries.
- [23](rules/maintenance.md#guideline-rule-23): Authorized email: Brando's signed-in account (mail connector, else uutils SMTP); BCC three inboxes, sender and To included; visible CC only on request; `drafted with <agent>` sign-off; “send” means send.
- [24](rules/maintenance.md#guideline-rule-24): Paper PDFs follow mandatory Rule 35.
- [25](rules/research.md#guideline-rule-25): VeriBench/VB private: >0.98 saturated; ≤0.9 good, ≤0.5 great, 0 best. "Harsh metric", N tasks, ASCII, harness. vb-priv: SYNC.md. Any metric ≥~0.98: solved (heuristic). [Set names](workflows/vb-sets.md).

## Authorized sign-in and verification codes

For an authorized account task, read [Rule 34](rules/services.md#trigger-rule-34): verify account, existing session or matching saved login and current challenge codes; keep credentials transient. Sign-in does not authorize unrelated transactions or messages.

## Machine Configs

Host routes: [catalog](CATALOG.md#machine-configs): [Mac](machine/mac.md), [SNAP](machine/snap.md), [Sherlock](machine/sherlock-agent-access.md), [FarmShare](machine/farmshare.md), [other agent clients](machine/agent-clis.md). Do not load unrelated hosts.

## Workflows

Use matching trigger links first. The [workflow catalog](CATALOG.md#workflows) indexes detailed procedures; [instruction maintenance](docs/instruction-audit/README.md) records the size budgets and client compatibility.

## Writing

The [writing catalog](CATALOG.md#writing) routes paper, blog and announcement work. Colocate all artifacts for a project/event; do not split them into top-level directories by file type.

## Abbreviations

`ac` = agents-config; `cc` = Claude Code. [Launcher/profile aliases](rules/services.md#abbreviations) are labels, not proof of account access or independent budget.

## Collaborators / Contact roster

Before addressing/assigning a person, resolve identity through [contacts](personal/contacts.md) and the [roster route](rules/services.md#collaborators--contact-roster).

## SNAP watcher reauth & reboot persistence (2026-04)

[Watcher reference](rules/hosts.md#snap-watcher-reauth--reboot-persistence-2026-04).

6. **Refresh configuration.** Follow the task-start/hourly refresh above, reread relevant changes, and preserve other owners’ work. Shared edits belong in both entry points. Review remains opt-in under Hard Rule 3. [Details](rules/maintenance.md#hard-rule-6)

7. **Keep clients current.** Use the installed package manager and the supported update hook; never assume npm. Do not install/use the deprecated Gemini CLI. [Details](rules/maintenance.md#hard-rule-7)

8. **Models, budgets and acceptance.** Masters: Codex `gpt-6-astra` / `ultra`; Claude `claude-fable-5-1` / `max`. Keep configured defaults; explicitly select proportionate execution workers (experiment selection: Guideline 19). Verify actual models/efforts and billing route (subscription or in-scope provider key). Never buy credits, enable new charges or weaken acceptance to recover. Required models/families and scientific pins remain binding. Before dispatch/review, read this detail and Rule 48. [Details](rules/safety-and-models.md#hard-rule-8)

9. **Model access: CLIs, subscriptions and provider keys are allowed.** Agents may wire Brando's existing provider keys into agent clients, write provider application programming interface (API) calls and run key-loading scripts without asking. Load keys at runtime, never print or commit them, keep each within its owner's scope and existing budgets, and cap and cost-estimate key-billed batch or unattended runs. [Details](rules/safety-and-models.md#hard-rule-9)

10. **Explain terminology.** Expand every acronym, metric symbol and project-specific term on first use in each response, chat included; use descriptive names, not opaque internal labels. For Brando, a code may lead if a short gloss follows on first use. [Details](rules/responses.md#hard-rule-10)

11. **Numbers with verdicts.** Compact entries link full statistics (Rule 4). Give measured values, scales, denominators/splits, threshold sources, missing measurements. Statistical headlines need 95% intervals (resampling unit, limits) and `x [lo, hi] p-val=Z` (named test/null or `p-val=n/a`). Report correlations individually; when interpreting score levels, add absolute agreement and mean bias (judge minus human, positive = lenient) with both means. Give repeated-score variability/counts. Existing data only; read the statistics workflow first. Research precision (10-24-2026): read settings, definitions, numbers from the repo, run records or paper; `unknown` only after a named-path search (in caption). VeriBench tables carry a Pi + best open-weight row. [Details](rules/responses.md#hard-rule-11)

## Guidelines (best practices)

- [14](rules/maintenance.md#guideline-rule-14): Complete direct authorized requests; do not ask again for already-authorized actions.
- [15](rules/maintenance.md#guideline-rule-15): Read only task-relevant referenced docs.
- [16](rules/maintenance.md#guideline-rule-16): Keep index, README and paths accurate; mirror shared entry bodies; verify actual host instruction files and reload state.
- [17](rules/responses.md#guideline-rule-17): Use anchored paths in prose and commands.
- [18](rules/maintenance.md#guideline-rule-18): Use `ls -la` for configuration/credential directories.
- [19](rules/research.md#guideline-rule-19): Select experiment models/judges by capability, total cost and validation; preserve pins.
- [20](rules/responses.md#guideline-rule-20): Messages/drafts as Brando use his concise first-person voice; email includes required routing/signature.
- [21](rules/maintenance.md#guideline-rule-21): Check `~/keys/` for credentials, model-provider keys included, before asking; keep values transient.
- [22](rules/maintenance.md#guideline-rule-22): Let the Node version manager control its path; avoid hardcoded versioned PATH entries.
- [23](rules/maintenance.md#guideline-rule-23): Authorized email: Brando's signed-in account (mail connector, else uutils SMTP); BCC three inboxes, sender and To included; visible CC only on request; `drafted with <agent>` sign-off; “send” means send.
- [24](rules/maintenance.md#guideline-rule-24): Paper PDFs follow mandatory Rule 35.
- [25](rules/research.md#guideline-rule-25): VeriBench/VB private: >0.98 saturated; ≤0.9 good, ≤0.5 great, 0 best. "Harsh metric", N tasks, ASCII, harness. vb-priv: SYNC.md. Any metric ≥~0.98: solved (heuristic). [Set names](workflows/vb-sets.md).

For an authorized account task, read [Rule 34](rules/services.md#trigger-rule-34): verify account, existing session or matching saved login and current challenge codes; keep credentials transient. Sign-in does not authorize unrelated transactions or messages.

Use matching trigger links first. The [workflow catalog](CATALOG.md#workflows) indexes detailed procedures; [instruction maintenance](docs/instruction-audit/README.md) records the size budgets and client compatibility.

The [writing catalog](CATALOG.md#writing) routes paper, blog and announcement work. Colocate all artifacts for a project/event; do not split them into top-level directories by file type.

`ac` = agents-config; `cc` = Claude Code. [Launcher/profile aliases](rules/services.md#abbreviations) are labels, not proof of account access or independent budget.

################ experiments/05_fresh_local_prover_target_judges/PROTOCOL.md
     1	<!-- TLDR: A capped local feasibility condition tests fresh specification outputs and two identified judge configurations without replacing the blocked frontier protocol. -->
     2	# Prospective local feasibility protocol
     3	
     4	Status, 11-06-2026: four source contexts and 15 integrity controls passed; freezing before the first model call. This protocol is distinct from experiment04's future 64-task evaluation and VeriBench experiment169's Pi/Gemini condition. Their owners, manifests, budgets, failures and watches are unchanged.
     5	
     6	## Question and scope
     7	
     8	Can an end-to-end statement-only pipeline produce checked bounded-prover outcomes and explicit probability forecasts on newly generated formal specifications? This pilot tests the pipeline and describes forecast error. Four purposively selected task families cannot establish a validated replacement, a frontier comparison or population-wide accuracy. Task selection favored two-function interfaces whose pinned source169 contexts round-trip exactly, have no representation adapter and have standard-axiom source witnesses. Source169 still has 14 emitted and 86 unresolved among all 100 pairs. This study does not inherit a 14-only denominator or call those outputs fresh.
     9	
    10	There are four source tasks, two statement-generator configurations per task, eight fresh artifacts, two judge configurations, one primary forecast per artifact/judge, and three forecasts on each of two preselected artifacts (T01/G0 and T03/G1). Thus T=4, A=2, J=2, primary K=1, repeat K=3 on two artifacts, and R=1 bounded prover search per fresh artifact. The two generator configurations and two judge configurations share one local backbone; they are not independent model families.
    11	
    12	The source families are string length, prefix filtering, URI permission and same-origin comparison. Their Python and gold are pinned source snapshots associated with source169, not a new full-release solver run. The generator receives only Python plus the declared public two-function interface (functional and imperative versions), and returns a Lean proposition about those abstract functions. It does not implement or prove a program. Internal/reference implementation scores are unmeasured and inapplicable to this restricted statement-authoring task. All eight initial cells stay in the ledger, including malformed statements, transport failure and unfinished cells.
    13	
    14	## New local target
    15	
    16	`P_local_qwen9_v1` is a new condition, not experiment169's Gemini/Pi target. The immutable goal is `∀ f0 f1, CandidateSpec f0 f1 → GoldSpec f0 f1`, where GoldSpec is the conjunction of every exported reference obligation, plus a separate `∃ f0 f1, CandidateSpec f0 f1` consistency goal. The functions are arbitrary, and no concrete implementation or source proof is available. Candidate proof bodies are irrelevant by construction: the target depends only on the emitted proposition. Fresh candidate consistency must be checked anew; the old source witness does not establish it.
    17	
    18	For each goal, try the fixed tactic battery, then at most one local-model proof term if the battery fails. There are no repair or retry calls. The event is 1 only if BOTH proofs pass independent strict kernel replay, exact goal-type equality, no newly added axioms and the allowed transitive axiom set `{propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound}`. A completed unsuccessful search is operational 0 and semantically unresolved. Model wall-time or output-token exhaustion, invalid returned proof text, and Lean proof-search/replay timeouts consume the bounded search and yield 0 when neither attempt succeeds; service, transport, process-death or trusted-context build failures remain missing. An infrastructure failure is recorded separately with target missing. A malformed candidate has no well-formed implication and is recorded as invalid, not semantic non-entailment. Independent checked counterexamples and consistency/refutation certificates are separate diagnostics; they never enter judge inputs.
    19	
    20	The checker reads a candidate module as data and re-adds its constants through Lean's kernel in a trusted process whose module path excludes that candidate. The reference, parser and replay modules are hash-protected. The trusted replay implementation is pinned to VeriBench ec1f9b2a4455549ba98a4fdf94c9d30bf3a0522d. Lean is 4.22.0; the installed Mathlib revision and manifest hash are recorded before execution. Proof-language filters supplement kernel checks. No credit relies on a free-form compiler log alone.
    21	
    22	## Integrity predictions before execution
    23	
    24	| Control | Expected observation |
    25	|---|---|
    26	| Source re-extraction | Four exact context hashes, round-trip equality and all reference names preserved |
    27	| True implication plus consistency witness | Both accepted |
    28	| Weak True specification | Counterexample checked; invented implication rejected |
    29	| Inconsistent specification | Implication can be proved, witness rejected, inconsistency checked; combined event 0 |
    30	| Wrong goal, unused added axiom, placeholder, native oracle, forged audit | Rejected |
    31	| Same statement with changed candidate proof metadata | Identical target hash |
    32	| Oracle forecast / half forecast / complemented outcome | Brier 0 / 0.25 / 1 |
    33	| Probability reproduction controls | Exact supplied 0.25 and 0.75 reproduced; failure stops new admissions |
    34	
    35	## Models, freezing and bounded execution
    36	
    37	All model roles use installed `qwen3.5:9b-q4_K_M`, digest `56671c2ab9385f9cfcb404638e32cd62d88e3501d44822208363c010179a3c90`, Ollama 0.40.8 on loopback, cloud disabled, no tools or internet. Thinking is explicitly false/true for G0/G1 and J0/J1; the prover uses true. Generator output limits are 1,024/2,048 tokens for G0/G1, judge limits are 256/2,048 for J0/J1, and prover limits are 2,048; thinking consumes that same output budget. The JSON configuration fixes prompts, temperature, seeds, token limits and parsing. Neither a provider key nor a personal model subscription funds these measured calls. Provider inference cost is $0; hardware time is measured, not claimed free of resource cost.
    38	
    39	Hard limits: 56 total reserved calls, 81,920 generated tokens by summed request limits, 180 seconds per model call, 60 seconds per Lean attempt, and four hours for the admitted local execution including finalization. Counts comprise 8 preflight calls, 8 generator calls, 24 forecasts and at most 16 prover calls. No automatic retries, fallback model or budget reset. Input context is capped at 8,192 tokens; requests record prompt hashes, actual model, completion reason, token counts and timing. Interrupted requests stay consumed and are not replayed.
    40	
    41	Freeze code/configuration and all cell identities before any model call. Freeze every judge prompt before generating target outcomes. Run all primary and repeat forecasts before target proof search; judge inputs contain Python, candidate statements, gold statements and the exact target protocol, without proofs, certificates, outcome bits or informative historical identifiers. Fresh outputs mean new statement artifacts and new judge responses; source tasks were previously exposed in experiment03. No fitted judge or score mapping is reused, and no task-family-held-out claim relative to experiment03 is made. There is no training or validation fit in this pilot, hence no selection on test outcomes and no claimed transfer to an unseen solver family.
    42	
    43	## Analysis and decision
    44	
    45	Primary descriptive measure: artifact-equal Brier loss on well-formed completed target cells, with every excluded/invalid/missing cell also listed. Compare fixed forecasts 0.5, 0.8 and 1.0; these are prespecified, not fitted to test outcomes. Report denominator, success prevalence, mean forecast, signed bias, mean absolute error, pairwise Brier difference, repeat variability and parsing/transport failures. Any interval resamples the four task families with paired configurations; it is descriptive and very imprecise, p-val=n/a. Do not treat eight artifacts as eight independent tasks.
    46	
    47	The expected positive result is a working checked pipeline with fresh probability outputs. The expected uncertainty is substantial: a small local model may fail Lean syntax/proofs, and the bounded target can fail on genuinely covering statements. A nontrivial forecast-agreement interpretation additionally needs both observed outcome classes and independently checked cases; otherwise report the degenerate result without a winner. No threshold from this pilot licenses deployment. The larger family-disjoint evaluation remains the separate experiment04 plan, with its exact prover/funding gates unresolved.
    48	
    49	One requested Claude Fable 5.1/max subscription review covers the final new code, condition, controls and results. Fix findings and run deterministic verification; do not start another independent review round.
    50	
    51	**TLDR-end:** [ttj: fresh local prover-target judges] Execute a bounded, independently checked local feasibility pilot on eight new specification artifacts. Preserve the separate frontier target, exposure limits and unfinished larger validation.

     2	# Fresh local prover-target judge results
     3	
     4	**Status, 11-06-2026: completed local feasibility test; no validated judge or winner.** The original thinking-enabled condition failed preflight. Its separately frozen non-thinking recovery finished all declared cells, but five statements were malformed and all three available bounded-prover outcomes were 0. Every parsed judge probability was also 0. The prespecified constant-zero baseline matches both judges.
     5	
     6	## Complete artifact ledger
     7	
     8	There were eight generation attempts on four purposively selected, previously exposed task families, with seven unique statement/context-source hashes. Only three artifacts were well formed: two duplicate statements from one task plus one statement from another. Thus there are two unique well-formed statements on two families, not eight independent test items.
     9	
    10	| Artifact | Statement/context | Prover outcome | J0 direct | J1 checklist |
    11	|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
    12	| T01_G0 | well formed | 0 | missing (token cap) | 0.0 |
    13	| T01_G1 | well formed; duplicate of T01_G0 | 0 | missing (token cap) | 0.0 |
    14	| T02_G0 | invalid syntax/type | missing | 0.0 | 0.0 |
    15	| T02_G1 | invalid syntax/type | missing | 0.0 | 0.0 |
    16	| T03_G0 | invalid syntax/type | missing | 0.0 | 0.0 |
    17	| T03_G1 | invalid syntax/type | missing | 0.0 | 0.0 |
    18	| T04_G0 | well formed | 0 | 0.0 | 0.0 |
    19	| T04_G1 | invalid syntax/type | missing | 0.0 | 0.0 |
    20	
    21	J0 and J1 are direct/checklist prompt configurations of the same Qwen3.5 9B Q4_K_M backbone, both with thinking disabled, capped at 256/1,024 output tokens. Generator prompts also share that backbone. Fourteen of sixteen forecasts parsed; the two missing J0 forecasts exhausted their frozen token limits and were not retried. Prefix-name syntax and extra nested lambdas account for the invalid contexts. They are not encoded as failed semantic implications.
    22	
    23	## Proper loss and missingness
    24	
    25	| Forecast | Available probability/outcome pairs | Conditional Brier | Full eight-artifact Brier bounds |
    26	|---|---:|---:|---|
    27	| J0 | 1/8 | 0.0000 | [0.0, 0.875] |
    28	| J1 | 3/8 | 0.0000 | [0.0, 0.625] |
    29	| Fixed 0.0 | 3/8 | 0.0000 | [0.0, 0.625] |
    30	| Fixed 0.5 | 3/8 | 0.2500 | [0.09375, 0.71875] |
    31	| Fixed 0.8 | 3/8 | 0.6400 | [0.24, 0.865] |
    32	| Fixed 1.0 | 3/8 | 1.0000 | [0.375, 1.0] |
    33	
    34	Conditional mean probability, mean target, signed bias and descriptive mean absolute error are all 0 for each judge, on only 1 paired artifact for J0 and 3 for J1. J0 versus J1 has only one shared available artifact. These zeros provide no evidence of useful discrimination: the outcome and forecast classes are constant, so Pearson, Spearman, Kendall and area under the receiver operating characteristic curve are unavailable. No repeated-forecast variability was measured in the recovery.
    35	
    36	Inferential intervals are unavailable. J0 has one observed family and J1 has two. Of 10,000 bootstrap draws, J0 retains 6,843 and drops 3,157 empty draws; J1 retains 9,375 and drops 625. The frozen four-family bootstrap mechanically returns [0,0] for observed judge losses; this is a degenerate resampling result, **not a precision or population-accuracy claim**. Empty resamples and their counts are explicit in [the detailed analysis](conditions/nonthinking_v2/results/analysis.json), p-val=n/a. The displayed bounds are hypothetical completed-loss bounds: if every missing cell had a defined binary target and forecast, its loss could lie anywhere in [0,1]. These are not confidence intervals, and malformed artifacts do not acquire a defined semantic score through this calculation. Missing outcomes or forecasts are never assigned zero. This support-count qualification was added after execution; the frozen analysis script and computed losses are unchanged. Brier is primary; absolute error is descriptive. No human ratings are used or replaced.
    37	
    38	## Target interpretation and controls
    39	
    40	The new local condition requires independently checked proofs of both candidate consistency and implication to every exported reference obligation. Its immutable statements, separate trusted kernel replay, exact goal types and axiom filter passed four source-context replays and fifteen designed controls. All six local-model proof attempts on the three valid artifacts returned parseable proof JSON but their proof terms were rejected; the fixed tactics also failed. Therefore these outcomes are bounded-search failures. A failed search alone says nothing conclusive about semantic entailment.
    41	
    42	Separate post-outcome diagnostics checked 2/2 counterexamples for the unique well-formed statements. Each certificate also supplies satisfying candidate functions, so these cases are consistent but do not imply the gold. The duplicate T01_G1 shares the exact T01_G0 statement/context hashes. These diagnostics never entered judge inputs and do not alter any operational target. See [diagnostic hashes](results/diagnostics.json).
    43	
    44	This is a distinct local prover condition, not VeriBench experiment169’s Pi/Gemini target. Source169 retains all 100 cases: 14 emitted contexts and 86 unresolved. This pilot selected four emitted cases for simple interfaces and makes no natural-population, frontier-model or unseen-task-family claim. The larger family-disjoint evaluation in [experiment04](../04_fresh_prover_target_judge_validation/PLAN.md) remains unfinished.
    45	
    46	## Shared accounting and audit
    47	
    48	Both conditions together reserved 46/56 calls and 49,152/81,920 requested output tokens, with 9,777 observed output tokens in terminal receipts. Provider charges were $0; measured execution elapsed 905.62 seconds (15.09 minutes), excluding preparation and review. Hardware use is not an end-to-end cost-saving result. No cap was reset and no failed measured cell was retried.
    49	
    50	The first condition used eight preflight calls, with six completed responses and two output-token failures; it generated no fresh artifact. The recovery used 38 calls: eight preflight, eight generation, sixteen forecast and six proof requests. Its preflight passed all eight checks. Actual model/server identities, combined token counts and thinking-character counts are retained; the server did not expose separate thinking-token counts.
    51	
    52	- [Shared summary](results/summary.json) and [receipt verification](results/verification.json).
    53	- [Original failed condition](results/v1_results.md) and its unchanged [freeze](sources/freeze.json).
    54	- [Recovery protocol](conditions/nonthinking_v2/PROTOCOL.md), [freeze](conditions/nonthinking_v2/sources/freeze.json) and [detailed report](conditions/nonthinking_v2/results.md).
    55	- [Reproduction runbook](RUNBOOK.md). Raw inputs, statements, proof attempts, model streams and certificates remain private.
    56	
    57	**TLDR-end:** [ttj: fresh local prover-target judges] The fresh local experiment is complete, with immutable target checks and full failure accounting. It did not identify a validated AI judge; a larger, distinct-outcome evaluation remains necessary.

     2	# Fresh local prover-target judge results
     3	
     4	**Status, 11-06-2026: completed local feasibility test; no validated judge or winner.** The original thinking-enabled condition failed preflight. Its separately frozen non-thinking recovery finished all declared cells, but five statements were malformed and all three available bounded-prover outcomes were 0. Every parsed judge probability was also 0. The prespecified constant-zero baseline matches both judges.
     5	
     6	## Complete artifact ledger
     7	
     8	There were eight generation attempts on four purposively selected, previously exposed task families, with seven unique statement/context-source hashes. Only three artifacts were well formed: two duplicate statements from one task plus one statement from another. Thus there are two unique well-formed statements on two families, not eight independent test items.
     9	
    10	| Artifact | Statement/context | Prover outcome | J0 direct | J1 checklist |
    11	|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
    12	| T01_G0 | well formed | 0 | missing (token cap) | 0.0 |
    13	| T01_G1 | well formed; duplicate of T01_G0 | 0 | missing (token cap) | 0.0 |
    14	| T02_G0 | invalid syntax/type | missing | 0.0 | 0.0 |
    15	| T02_G1 | invalid syntax/type | missing | 0.0 | 0.0 |
    16	| T03_G0 | invalid syntax/type | missing | 0.0 | 0.0 |
    17	| T03_G1 | invalid syntax/type | missing | 0.0 | 0.0 |
    18	| T04_G0 | well formed | 0 | 0.0 | 0.0 |
    19	| T04_G1 | invalid syntax/type | missing | 0.0 | 0.0 |
    20	
    21	J0 and J1 are direct/checklist prompt configurations of the same Qwen3.5 9B Q4_K_M backbone, both with thinking disabled, capped at 256/1,024 output tokens. Prefix-name syntax and extra nested lambdas account for the invalid contexts. They are not encoded as failed semantic implications.
    22	
    23	## Proper loss and missingness
    24	
    25	| Forecast | Available probability/outcome pairs | Conditional Brier | Full eight-artifact Brier bounds |
    26	|---|---:|---:|---|
    27	| J0 | 1/8 | 0.0000 | [0.0, 0.875] |
    28	| J1 | 3/8 | 0.0000 | [0.0, 0.625] |
    29	| Fixed 0.0 | 3/8 | 0.0000 | [0.0, 0.625] |
    30	| Fixed 0.5 | 3/8 | 0.2500 | [0.09375, 0.71875] |
    31	| Fixed 0.8 | 3/8 | 0.6400 | [0.24, 0.865] |
    32	| Fixed 1.0 | 3/8 | 1.0000 | [0.375, 1.0] |

J0 versus J1 has only one shared available artifact. These zeros provide no evidence of useful discrimination: the outcome and forecast classes are constant, so Pearson, Spearman, Kendall and area under the receiver operating characteristic curve are unavailable. No repeated-forecast variability was measured in the recovery.
    35	
    36	Inferential intervals are unavailable. J0 has one observed family and J1 has two. Of 10,000 bootstrap draws, J0 retains 6,843 and drops 3,157 empty draws; J1 retains 9,375 and drops 625. The frozen four-family bootstrap mechanically returns [0,0] for observed judge losses; this is a degenerate resampling result, **not a precision or population-accuracy claim**. Empty resamples and their counts are explicit in [the detailed analysis](conditions/nonthinking_v2/results/analysis.json), p-val=n/a. The displayed bounds are hypothetical completed-loss bounds: if every missing cell had a defined binary target and forecast, its loss could lie anywhere in [0,1]. These are not confidence intervals, and malformed artifacts do not acquire a defined semantic score through this calculation. Missing outcomes or forecasts are never assigned zero. The larger family-disjoint evaluation in [experiment04](../04_fresh_prover_target_judge_validation/PLAN.md) remains unfinished.

    47	
    48	Both conditions together reserved 46/56 calls and 49,152/81,920 requested output tokens, with 9,777 observed output tokens in terminal receipts. Provider charges were $0; measured execution elapsed 905.62 seconds (15.09 minutes), excluding preparation and review. Hardware use is not an end-to-end cost-saving result. No cap was reset and no failed measured cell was retried.

1	#!/usr/bin/env python3
     2	"""TLDR: Execute a hash-frozen, zero-provider-cost local pilot with durable no-retry call receipts."""
     3	import argparse
     4	import datetime
     5	import fcntl
     6	import hashlib
     7	import json
     8	import os
     9	import signal
    10	import subprocess
    11	import time
    12	import urllib.request
    13	import urllib.error
    14	from pathlib import Path
    15	from checker import Checker, ContextFailure, PRIVATE, ROOT, context, sha
    16	
    17	CONFIG=json.loads((ROOT/'config.json').read_text())
    18	
    19	class BudgetTimeout(TimeoutError): pass
    20	class IntegrityFailure(RuntimeError): pass
    21	
    22	def dump(path, value):
    23	    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True,exist_ok=True)
    24	    temporary=path.with_suffix(path.suffix+'.tmp')
    25	    temporary.write_text(json.dumps(value,indent=2,allow_nan=False)+'\n'); temporary.replace(path)
    26	
    27	def now(): return datetime.datetime.now(datetime.timezone.utc).isoformat()
    28	
    29	def read_api(path, payload=None):
    30	    raw=None if payload is None else json.dumps(payload).encode()
    31	    request=urllib.request.Request(CONFIG['endpoint']+'/api/'+path,data=raw,headers={'Content-Type':'application/json'})
    32	    return json.loads(urllib.request.urlopen(request,timeout=10).read())
    33	
    34	def check_runtime():
    35	    assert read_api('version')['version']==CONFIG['ollama_version']
    36	    models=read_api('tags')['models']
    37	    row=next(m for m in models if m['name']==CONFIG['model'])
    38	    assert row['digest']==CONFIG['model_digest']
    39	    return {'model':row['name'],'digest':row['digest'],'server_version':CONFIG['ollama_version']}
    40	
    41	def verify_freeze():
    42	    freeze=json.loads((ROOT/'sources/freeze.json').read_text())
    43	    assert sha((ROOT.parents[1]/'sources/freeze.json').read_bytes())==freeze['parent_freeze_sha256']
    44	    for file,digest in freeze['files'].items():
    45	        assert sha((ROOT/file).read_bytes())==digest, 'Frozen file changed: '+file
    46	    assert sha((PRIVATE/'cases.json').read_bytes())==freeze['private_case_manifest_sha256']
    47	    for row in json.loads((ROOT/'sources/provenance.json').read_text())['sources']:
    48	        assert sha((PRIVATE/row['destination']).read_bytes())==row['sha256']
    49	    for file,digest in freeze['runtime_dependencies'].items():
    50	        assert sha(Path(file).read_bytes())==digest, 'Runtime dependency changed: '+file
    51	    assert json.loads((ROOT/'results/target_checks.json').read_text())['all_pass']
    52	    return freeze
    53	
    54	def journal():
    55	    p=PRIVATE/'run_state.json'
    56	    if p.exists(): return json.loads(p.read_text())
    57	    state={'started_utc':now(),'started_epoch':time.time(),'calls':{},'phase':'preflight','status':'running'}
    58	    dump(p,state); return state
    59	
    60	def progress(state, phase):
    61	    state.update(updated_utc=now(),phase=phase,pid=os.getpid())
    62	    dump(PRIVATE/'run_state.json',state)
    63	    public={'phase':phase,'status':state['status'],'updated_utc':state['updated_utc'],
    64	            'reserved_calls':len(state['calls']), 'reserved_generated_tokens':sum(r['num_predict'] for r in state['calls'].values()),
    65	            'finished_calls':sum(r.get('status')=='completed' for r in state['calls'].values()),
    66	            'failed_or_interrupted_calls':sum(r.get('status') not in {'completed','reserved'} for r in state['calls'].values()),
    67	            'provider_cost_usd':0}
    68	    dump(ROOT/'results/live.json',public)
    69	
    70	def parse_json(text, field):
    71	    value=json.loads(text)
    72	    assert isinstance(value,dict)
    73	    if field=='probability':
    74	        q=value[field]; assert type(q) in {int,float} and 0<=q<=1
    75	        assert isinstance(value.get('reason'),str)
    76	    else: assert isinstance(value[field],str)
    77	    return value
    78	
    79	def call(identity, role, settings, messages, field, seed):
    80	    freeze=verify_freeze(); state=journal()
    81	    assert identity in freeze['planned_calls']
    82	    assert settings['num_predict']==freeze['planned_calls'][identity]['num_predict']
    83	    folder=PRIVATE/'calls'/identity
    84	    if identity in state['calls']:
    85	        result=folder/'receipt.json'
    86	        if result.exists(): return json.loads(result.read_text())
    87	        # A consumed request cannot be replayed after process death.

   154	def preflight():

   160	            results.append({'identity':r['identity'],'passed':passed,'kind':'probability_reproduction'})
   161	        for index,positive in enumerate([True,False]):
   162	            data=('The fixed tactic proves both goals by identity. CandidateSpec f = (∀ n : Nat, f n = n), GoldSpec f is identical; witness f = id.' if positive else
   163	                  'CandidateSpec f is False, GoldSpec f = (∀ n : Nat, f n = n). Implication is trivial, but the consistency goal ∃f, False is impossible in the trusted kernel.')

   170	def generate():

   174	        for g,settings in CONFIG['generator'].items():

   178	            item={'id':identity,'task_id':case['id'],'generator':g,'generation_status':r['status']}
   179	            if r['status']=='completed':

   262	def main():

1	#!/usr/bin/env python3
     2	"""TLDR: Bind statement-only inputs to fixed goals and independently replay every credited proof."""
     3	import hashlib
     4	import json
     5	import os
     6	import re
     7	import secrets
     8	import shutil
     9	import subprocess
    10	import tempfile
    11	from pathlib import Path
    12	
    13	ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
    14	PRIVATE = ROOT.parents[3] / 'private/fresh_prover_target/v2'
    15	DEPENDENCIES = PRIVATE / 'dependencies'
    16	LEAN_PROJECT = Path.home() / 'veribench/veribench_dataset/lean_src'
    17	AXIOMS = {'propext', 'Classical.choice', 'Quot.sound'}
    18	SPEC_ONLY = '''import Mathlib
    19	import Lean
    20	open Lean Elab Command
    21	elab "specification " n:ident " : " ty:term " := " body:str : command => do
    22	  let env ← getEnv
    23	  match Parser.runParserCategory env `term body.getString with
    24	  | .error msg => throwError "Specification must be exactly one Lean term: {msg}"
    25	  | .ok term =>
    26	    let parsed : TSyntax `term := ⟨term⟩
    27	    let cmd ← `(def $n : $ty := $parsed)
    28	    elabCommand cmd
    29	'''
    30	FORBIDDEN = {'sorry', 'admit', 'sorryAx', 'native_decide', 'axiom', 'run_tac', 'set_option',
    31	             'macro', 'macro_rules', 'elab', 'elab_rules', 'unsafe', 'partial', 'import',
    32	             'opaque', 'implemented_by', 'extern', 'init_quot', 'addDecl', 'skipKernelTC'}
    33	
    34	def sha(data): return hashlib.sha256(data).hexdigest()
    35	
    36	def blocked(text, specification=False):
    37	    identifiers = set(re.findall(r"[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z_0-9.']*", text))
    38	    words = FORBIDDEN | ({'by', 'GoldSpec', 'Coverage', 'Nonvacuous', 'Context'} if specification else set())
    39	    return sorted(t for t in words if any(i == t or i.split('.')[-1] == t for i in identifiers))
    40	
    41	def context(case, specification):
    42	    assert isinstance(specification, str) and 0 < len(specification.encode()) <= 12000
    43	    if blocked(specification, True): raise ValueError('Forbidden specification syntax')
    44	    gold = (PRIVATE/'cases'/case['id']/'GoldDefinition.txt').read_text()
    45	    assert sha(gold.encode()) == case['gold_definition_sha256']
    46	    slots = case['slots']
    47	    assert len(slots) == 2 and [s['binder'] for s in slots] == ['f0', 'f1']
    48	    ty = ' → '.join('('+s['typePP']+')' for s in slots) + ' → Prop'
    49	    signature = case['signature']
    50	    return ('import SpecOnly\nnamespace Natural\n' + gold + '\n' +
    51	            'specification AgentSpec : '+ty+' := '+json.dumps('fun f0 f1 => '+specification, ensure_ascii=False)+'\n'+
    52	            'def Coverage : Prop := ∀ '+signature+', AgentSpec f0 f1 → GoldSpec f0 f1\n'+
    53	            'def Nonvacuous : Prop := ∃ '+signature+', AgentSpec f0 f1\n'+
    54	            'def Counterexample : Prop := ∃ '+signature+', AgentSpec f0 f1 ∧ ¬ GoldSpec f0 f1\n'+
    55	            'end Natural\n')
    56	
    57	class ContextFailure(ValueError):
    58	    def __init__(self, category, message):
    59	        super().__init__(message)
    60	        self.category=category
    61	
    62	class Checker:
    63	    def __init__(self, directory, source):
    64	        self.root = Path(directory).resolve()
    65	        self.trusted = self.root/'trusted'
    66	        self.trusted.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    67	        self.env = {k:v for k,v in os.environ.items() if not re.search('KEY|TOKEN|SECRET|PASSWORD|CREDENTIAL|AUTH|COOKIE|SESSION', k, re.I)}
    68	        self.lean = subprocess.check_output(['elan','which','lean'],cwd=LEAN_PROJECT,text=True,env=self.env).strip()
    69	        self.version = subprocess.check_output([self.lean,'--version'],text=True,env=self.env).strip()
    70	        assert '4.22.0' in self.version
    71	        assert (LEAN_PROJECT/'lean-toolchain').read_text().strip() == 'leanprover/lean4:v4.22.0'
    72	        self.lib = subprocess.check_output(['lake','env','printenv','LEAN_PATH'],cwd=LEAN_PROJECT,text=True,env=self.env).strip().splitlines()[-1]
    73	        self.path = str(self.trusted)+':'+self.lib
    74	        (self.trusted/'SpecOnly.lean').write_text(SPEC_ONLY)
    75	        (self.trusted/'Context.lean').write_text(source)
    76	        for name in ['ProofOnly', 'KernelReplayStrictSupport']:
    77	            shutil.copyfile(DEPENDENCIES/(name+'.lean'), self.trusted/(name+'.lean'))
    78	        self.builds = {}
    79	        for name in ['SpecOnly','Context','ProofOnly','KernelReplayStrictSupport']:
    80	            result = self.compile(self.trusted/(name+'.lean'), self.path, True)
    81	            self.builds[name] = result
    82	            if result['exit_code']:
    83	                category='invalid_context' if name=='Context' and result['exit_code']==1 else 'infrastructure_missing'
    84	                (self.root/'build_failure.json').write_text(json.dumps(self.builds,indent=2)+'\n')
    85	                raise ContextFailure(category,f'{name} failed: '+result['output'][-1800:])
    86	        self.protected = self.hashes()
    87	
    88	    def hashes(self):
    89	        return {p.name:sha(p.read_bytes()) for p in self.trusted.iterdir() if p.suffix in {'.lean','.olean'} and not p.name.startswith('Replay_')}
    90	
    91	    def compile(self, file, search_path, output=False, isolate=False):
    92	        cmd=[self.lean,'-j1','-DmaxHeartbeats=400000','-DElab.async=false','-R',str(file.parent)]
    93	        if output: cmd += ['-o',str(file.with_suffix('.olean'))]
    94	        cmd.append(str(file))
    95	        if isolate:
    96	            assert Path('/usr/bin/sandbox-exec').exists()
    97	            profile='(version 1)(allow default)(deny network*)(deny file-write*)(allow file-write* (subpath '+json.dumps(str(file.parent.resolve()))+'))'
    98	            cmd=['/usr/bin/sandbox-exec','-p',profile]+cmd
    99	        try:
   100	            p=subprocess.run(cmd,cwd=LEAN_PROJECT,env=dict(self.env,LEAN_PATH=search_path),text=True,capture_output=True,timeout=60)
   101	            return {'exit_code':p.returncode,'output':p.stdout+p.stderr,'argv':cmd,'timeout_seconds':60}
   102	        except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
   103	            return {'exit_code':124,'output':'Compile time limit 60 seconds','argv':cmd,'timeout_seconds':60}
   104	
   105	    def check(self, proof, target):
   106	        if not isinstance(proof,str) or not proof.strip() or len(proof.encode())>20000:
   107	            return {'accepted':False,'status':'invalid_proof_size'}
   108	        rejected=blocked(proof)
   109	        if rejected: return {'accepted':False,'status':'proof_guard_rejected','tokens':rejected}
   110	        source='import Context\nimport ProofOnly\ncandidate claim : '+target+' := '+json.dumps(proof,ensure_ascii=False)+'\n'
   111	        return self.check_raw(source,target)
   112	
   113	    def check_raw(self, source, target):
   114	        """Raw declarations are used only by adversarial checker controls, never model output."""
   115	        assert target in {'Natural.Coverage','Natural.Nonvacuous','Natural.Counterexample','Natural.Inconsistent','True','False'}
   116	        assert self.hashes()==self.protected
   117	        directory=Path(tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix='candidate_',dir=self.root))
   118	        candidate=directory/'Candidate.lean'; candidate.write_text(source)
   119	        result={'target':target,'candidate_sha256':sha(source.encode()),'accepted':False}
   120	        compiled=self.compile(candidate,str(directory)+':'+self.path,True,True)
   121	        result['compile']=compiled
   122	        if compiled['exit_code']:
   123	            result['status']='search_timeout' if compiled['exit_code']==124 else 'infrastructure_failure' if compiled['exit_code']<0 else 'proof_rejected'
   124	        else:
   125	            artifact=candidate.with_suffix('.olean'); original=sha(artifact.read_bytes())
   126	            nonce=secrets.token_hex(24)
   127	            replay=self.trusted/('Replay_'+nonce+'.lean')
   128	            replay.write_text('import Context\nimport KernelReplayStrictSupport\n#vb_strict_kernel_replay '+json.dumps(nonce)+' '+json.dumps(str(artifact))+' claim : '+target+'\n')
   129	            try: checked=self.compile(replay,self.path)
   130	            finally: replay.unlink(missing_ok=True)
   131	            records=[]
   132	            for line in checked['output'].splitlines():
   133	                if 'VB169_STRICT_KERNEL_REPLAY_JSON ' in line:
   134	                    try: r=json.loads(line.split('VB169_STRICT_KERNEL_REPLAY_JSON ',1)[1])
   135	                    except json.JSONDecodeError: continue
   136	                    if r.get('nonce')==nonce: records.append(r)
   137	            r=records[0] if len(records)==1 else {}
   138	            result.update({'replay':checked,'records':records,'olean_sha256':original,'olean_unchanged':sha(artifact.read_bytes())==original})
   139	            result['accepted']=bool(checked['exit_code']==0 and r.get('replayed') and r.get('isTheorem') and r.get('typeExact') and not r.get('collisions') and set(r.get('axioms',[]))<=AXIOMS and result['olean_unchanged'])
   140	            result['status']='accepted' if result['accepted'] else 'search_timeout' if checked['exit_code']==124 else 'infrastructure_failure' if checked['exit_code']<0 else 'kernel_replay_rejected'
   141	        result['protected_intact']=self.hashes()==self.protected
   142	        assert result['protected_intact']
   143	        (directory/'receipt.json').write_text(json.dumps(result,indent=2)+'\n')
   144	        return result

    70	        assert '4.22.0' in self.version
    71	        assert (LEAN_PROJECT/'lean-toolchain').read_text().strip() == 'leanprover/lean4:v4.22.0'
    72	        self.lib = subprocess.check_output(['lake','env','printenv','LEAN_PATH'],cwd=LEAN_PROJECT,text=True,env=self.env).strip().splitlines()[-1]

    76	        for name in ['ProofOnly', 'KernelReplayStrictSupport']:
    77	            shutil.copyfile(DEPENDENCIES/(name+'.lean'), self.trusted/(name+'.lean'))

    90	
    91	    def compile(self, file, search_path, output=False, isolate=False):
    92	        cmd=[self.lean,'-j1','-DmaxHeartbeats=400000','-DElab.async=false','-R',str(file.parent)]

    97	            profile='(version 1)(allow default)(deny network*)(deny file-write*)(allow file-write* (subpath '+json.dumps(str(file.parent.resolve()))+'))'

   105	    def check(self, proof, target):

    14	INF_REV = '36a4d8b54aca7133e381601f285ffa4b7f82b28c'

    20	def digest(data):

    23	def save(path, data):

    33	
    34	def blob(repo, revision, name):
    35	    return subprocess.check_output(['git', '-C', str(repo), 'show', revision + ':' + name])
    36	
    37	def main():
    38	    provenance = []
    39	    def snapshot(repo, revision, source, destination):
    40	        data = blob(repo, revision, source)
    41	        save(PRIVATE / destination, data)
    42	        provenance.append({'repository': repo.name, 'revision': revision, 'source': source,
    43	                           'destination': destination, 'sha256': digest(data), 'bytes': len(data)})
    44	        return data
    45	    paths = {
    46	        'scripts/vb169_service/trusted_checker.py': 'dependencies/trusted_checker.py',
    47	        'scripts/lean/KernelReplayStrictSupport.lean': 'dependencies/KernelReplayStrictSupport.lean',

    52	    for name, dest in paths.items(): snapshot(VB, VB_REV, E169 + name, dest)
    53	    snapshot(INF, INF_REV, E13 + 'scripts/ProofOnly.lean', 'dependencies/ProofOnly.lean')
    54	    ledger = json.loads((PRIVATE/'source/full100_ledger.json').read_text())['rows']
    55	    cases = []
    56	    for number, (module, family) in enumerate(SELECTION):
    57	        r = next(row for row in ledger if row['module'] == module)
    58	        assert r['status'] == 'emitted' and not r['witness']['axioms_outside_allowlist']
    59	        assert r['match_tier'] != 'declared_adapter'
    60	        assert r['lean_vs_source_names_agree']['gold'] and r['lean_vs_source_names_agree']['agent']
    61	        assert len(r['extraction']['slots']) == 2
    62	        ident = f'T{number+1:02}'

    66	        source_revision = r['repo_commit']

    68	        agent = snapshot(VB, source_revision, r['solver_path'], stem+'OldAgentSource.lean')

    83	               'source_receipt': r}
    84	        cases.append(row)

    92	if __name__ == '__main__': main()

     1	#!/usr/bin/env python3
     2	"""TLDR: Re-extract pinned source contexts and test strict fixed-goal acceptance before model calls."""
     3	import concurrent.futures
     4	import importlib.util
     5	import json
     6	from pathlib import Path

     9	def load_exporter():

    12	    module=importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec); spec.loader.exec_module(module)
    13	    module.REPO=Path.home()/'veribench'
    14	    module.ADAPTERS=PRIVATE/'absent_adapters'
    15	    return module
    16	
    17	def reextract():
    18	    ex=load_exporter(); tool=ex.Toolchain(ex.PROJECT)
    19	    support=PRIVATE/'dependencies'
    20	    compiled=tool.compile(support/'ExtractSupport.lean',[support],olean=True)
    21	    assert compiled['exit_code']==0,compiled['output']
    22	    cases=json.loads((PRIVATE/'cases.json').read_text())
    23	    def one(case):
    24	        old=case['source_receipt']
    25	        row={'id':old['id'],'module':old['module'],'task':old['task'],'solver':old['solver'],
    26	             'category':old['category'],'gold_path':old['gold_path'],
    27	             'gold_current_head_sha256':old['gold_sha256'],'source_path':old['solver_path'],
    28	             'source_sha256':old['solver_sha256']}
    29	        receipt=ex.run_case(row,tool,PRIVATE/'source_replay',old['repo_commit'],support)
    30	        assert receipt['status']=='emitted',receipt['reasons']
    31	        assert receipt['context_sha256']==old['context_sha256']
    32	        assert not receipt['witness']['axioms_outside_allowlist']
    33	        return {'id':case['id'],'status':receipt['status'],'context_sha256':receipt['context_sha256'],
    34	                'roundtrip_exact':receipt['roundtrip']['ok'], 'witness_standard_axioms':True,
    35	                'all_source_names_match':receipt['lean_vs_source_names_agree']['gold'] and receipt['lean_vs_source_names_agree']['agent']}
    36	    with concurrent.futures.ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=2) as pool:
    37	        results=list(pool.map(one,cases))
    38	    return results
    39	
    40	def controls():
    41	    gold='def GoldSpec (f : Nat → Nat) : Prop := ∀ n, f n = n\n'
    42	    def fixture(agent):
    43	        return ('import Mathlib\nnamespace Natural\n'+gold+
    44	                'def AgentSpec (f : Nat → Nat) : Prop := '+agent+'\n'+
    45	                'def Coverage : Prop := ∀ f, AgentSpec f → GoldSpec f\n'+
    46	                'def Nonvacuous : Prop := ∃ f, AgentSpec f\n'+
    47	                'def Counterexample : Prop := ∃ f, AgentSpec f ∧ ¬ GoldSpec f\n'+
    48	                'def Inconsistent : Prop := ¬ Nonvacuous\nend Natural\n')
    49	    good=Checker(PRIVATE/'target_controls/good',fixture('∀ n, f n = n'))
    50	    weak=Checker(PRIVATE/'target_controls/weak',fixture('True'))
    51	    inconsistent=Checker(PRIVATE/'target_controls/inconsistent',fixture('False'))
    52	    checks=[]
    53	    def check(name,checker,proof,target,expected,raw=False):
    54	        result=checker.check_raw(proof,target) if raw else checker.check(proof,target)
    55	        assert result['accepted']==expected,(name,result)
    56	        checks.append({'name':name,'expected':expected,'accepted':result['accepted'],'status':result['status']})
    57	    check('valid_implication',good,'by intro f h; exact h','Natural.Coverage',True)
    58	    check('consistency_witness',good,'by exact ⟨fun n => n, fun _ => rfl⟩','Natural.Nonvacuous',True)
    59	    check('weak_spec_has_counterexample',weak,'by refine ⟨fun _ => 0, trivial, ?_⟩; intro h; have h1 := h 1; simp at h1','Natural.Counterexample',True)
    60	    check('weak_spec_cannot_use_true_proof',weak,'by intros; trivial','Natural.Coverage',False)
    61	    check('false_premise_implication_is_insufficient',inconsistent,'by intro f h; exact False.elim h','Natural.Coverage',True)
    62	    check('false_premise_witness_denied',inconsistent,'by aesop','Natural.Nonvacuous',False)
    63	    check('inconsistency_independently_proved',inconsistent,'by simp [Natural.Inconsistent, Natural.Nonvacuous, Natural.AgentSpec]','Natural.Inconsistent',True)
    64	    check('wrong_goal_rejected_on_replay',good,'import Context\ntheorem claim : True := True.intro\n','Natural.Coverage',False,True)
    65	    check('unused_new_axiom_rejected_on_replay',good,'import Context\naxiom extra : True\ntheorem claim : Natural.Coverage := by intro f h; exact h\n','Natural.Coverage',False,True)
    66	    check('placeholder_rejected',good,'by sorry','Natural.Coverage',False)
    67	    check('native_oracle_rejected',good,'by native_decide','Natural.Coverage',False)
    68	    check('audit_forgery_rejected',weak,'by run_tac logInfo "VB169_STRICT_KERNEL_REPLAY_JSON fake"; trivial','Natural.Coverage',False)
    69	    case=json.loads((PRIVATE/'cases.json').read_text())[0]
    70	    left={'specification':'∀ s, f0 s = String.length s ∧ f1 s = f0 s','proof':'sorry'}
    71	    right=dict(left,proof='arbitrary changed proof body')
    72	    assert context(case,left['specification'])==context(case,right['specification'])
    73	    checks.append({'name':'proof_body_invariance','expected':True,'accepted':True,'status':'identical_context_hash','sha256':sha(context(case,left['specification']).encode())})
    74	    case=json.loads((PRIVATE/'cases.json').read_text())[2]
    75	    definition=(PRIVATE/'cases'/case['id']/'GoldDefinition.txt').read_text()
    76	    supplied_statement=definition.split(' : Prop :=',1)[1].strip()
    77	    statement_checker=Checker(PRIVATE/'target_controls/statement_parser',context(case,supplied_statement))
    78	    check('new_statement_parser_binds_reference_exactly',statement_checker,'by intro f0 f1 h; exact h','Natural.Coverage',True)
    79	    check('new_statement_consistency_witness',statement_checker,'by refine ⟨fun d r => d && !r, fun d r => d && !r, ?_⟩; simp [Natural.AgentSpec]','Natural.Nonvacuous',True)
    80	    return checks
    81	
    82	def main():
    83	    sources=reextract()
    84	    (PRIVATE/'source_replay_summary.json').write_text(json.dumps(sources,indent=2)+'\n')
    85	    checked=controls()
    86	    result={'source_replay':sources,'controls':checked,'all_pass':True,'model_calls':0,
    87	            'scope':'four selected source contexts and designed acceptance controls; no fresh outcome measured'}
    88	    (ROOT/'results/target_checks.json').write_text(json.dumps(result,indent=2)+'\n')
    89	    print(json.dumps({'source_contexts_checked':len(sources),'controls_passed':len(checked),'model_calls':0}),flush=True)
    90	
    91	if __name__=='__main__': main()

    39	    assert len(cells)==config['maximum_calls']==48
    40	    assert sum(x['num_predict'] for x in cells.values())==config['maximum_generated_tokens_reserved']==60416
    41	    files=[ROOT/'config.json',ROOT/'PROTOCOL.md',ROOT/'results/target_checks.json',ROOT/'sources/provenance.json']

    45	           'runtime_dependencies':runtime,'mathlib_revision':revision,

    48	           'private_case_manifest_sha256':sha((PRIVATE/'cases.json').read_bytes()),'planned_calls':cells,
    49	           'code_commit_before_freeze':subprocess.check_output(['git','rev-parse','HEAD'],text=True).strip()}
    50	    (ROOT/'sources/freeze.json').write_text(json.dumps(value,indent=2)+'\n')

=== ProofOnly.lean ===
     1	/- Parse a candidate as one proof term and bind it to an immutable, separately constructed goal. -/
     2	import Mathlib
     3	import Lean
     4	open Lean Elab Command
     5

import json
from pathlib import Path
P=Path('private/fresh_prover_target')
for tag,priv in [('v1',P),('v2',P/'v2')]:
    print('=====',tag,'receipts')
    s=json.loads((priv/'run_state.json').read_text())
    for ident,r in s['calls'].items():
        req=json.loads((priv/'calls'/ident/'request.json').read_bytes())
        parsed=r.get('parsed')
        pv=None
        if parsed:
            pv=parsed.get('probability') if 'probability' in parsed else ('spec_len=%d'%len(parsed['specification']) if 'specification' in parsed else 'proof_len=%d'%len(parsed['proof']))
        print(f"{ident:26} {r['role']:12} {r['status']:9} done={r.get('done_reason')!s:6} eval={r.get('eval_count')!s:5}/{r['num_predict']:5} pe={r.get('prompt_eval_count')!s:5} think={req['think']!s:5} thinkchars={r.get('thinking_characters')!s:6} fail={r.get('failure_category')!s:20} seed={r['seed']} t={r['seconds']:.1f} start={r['started_utc'][11:19]} end={r['finished_utc'][11:19]} parsed={pv}")
        assert req['model']=='qwen3.5:9b-q4_K_M' and req['options']['num_predict']==r['num_predict'] and req['options']['seed']==r['seed'] and req['options']['num_ctx']==8192 and req['options']['temperature']==0.2
        assert req['messages'][0]['role']=='system' and req['messages'][1]['role']=='user' and len(req['messages'])==2
EOF

import json

    print(f"{f['artifact']} {f['judge']} rep={f['repetition']} status={f['status']} p={f['probability']} stmt={str(f.get('statement_sha256'))[:8]} ctx={str(f.get('context_sha256'))[:8]} gold={f['gold_definition_sha256'][:8]} in={str(f.get('input_sha256'))[:8]} reason={str(f.get('reason'))[:150]!r}")
print()
print('=== artifact specifications (private, review only) ===')
for a in json.loads((P/'artifacts.json').read_text()):
    print(f"--- {a['id']} status={a['generation_status']} stmt={a.get('statement_sha256','')[:8]} ctx={a.get('context_sha256','')[:8]} invalid={a.get('invalid_reason')}")
    print(repr(a.get('specification')))
print()
print('=== diagnostic proposals (private) ===')
d=json.loads((P/'diagnostic_proposals.json').read_text())
for k,v in d.items(): print(k,':',repr(v))
for ident in d:
    r=json.loads((P/'diagnostics'/ident/'result.json').read_text())
    print(ident,'accepted=',r['accepted'],'status=',r['status'],'olean_unchanged=',r.get('olean_unchanged'),'protected=',r.get('protected_intact'))
    for rec in r.get('records',[]): print('   record:',{k:rec[k] for k in ['replayed','isTheorem','typeExact','typeDefEq','axioms','collisions','candidateImports','candidateConstants','error']})
print()
print('=== model proof texts (private) ===')
for t in json.loads((P/'targets.json').read_text()):
    for g,dd in t.get('goals',{}).items():
        if 'model_proof' in dd:
            print(t['artifact'],g,'->',repr(dd['model_proof'].get('candidate_sha256','')[:8]))
            cs=json.loads((P/'calls'/('prove_'+t['artifact']+'_'+('0' if g.endswith('Nonvacuous') else '1'))/'receipt.json').read_text())
            print('   proof:',repr(cs['parsed']['proof'][:400]))

echo "=== review launch metadata ===" && cat private/fresh_prover_target/review/launch.json private/fresh_prover_target/review/worker.json private/fresh_prover_target/review/active_cli_evidence.json private/fresh_prover_target/review/reviewed_commit.txt && echo && echo "=== hash consistency ===" && python3 -I - <<'EOF'
import json,hashlib
from pathlib import Path
sha=lambda b:hashlib.sha256(b).hexdigest()
E=Path('experiments/05_fresh_local_prover_target_judges'); V=E/'conditions/nonthinking_v2'
P=Path('private/fresh_prover_target'); P2=P/'v2'
ok=lambda name,cond:print(('PASS ' if cond else 'FAIL ')+name)
ok('generation_receipt sha == v2/artifacts.json', json.load(open(V/'results/generation_receipt.json'))['private_artifact_sha256']==sha((P2/'artifacts.json').read_bytes()))
ok('forecast_receipt sha == v2/forecasts.json', json.load(open(V/'results/forecast_receipt.json'))['sha256']==sha((P2/'forecasts.json').read_bytes()))
ok('target_receipt sha == v2/targets.json', json.load(open(V/'results/target_receipt.json'))['sha256']==sha((P2/'targets.json').read_bytes()))
arts=json.load(open(P2/'artifacts.json'))
ok('artifact_hashes.json == projection of private artifacts', json.load(open(V/'results/artifact_hashes.json'))==[{k:v for k,v in a.items() if k not in {'specification','context_source'}} for a in arts])
ok('v2 analysis.json inputs == private file hashes', all(json.load(open(V/'results/analysis.json'))['inputs'][n]==sha((P2/n).read_bytes()) for n in ['artifacts.json','forecasts.json','targets.json','run_state.json','done.json']))
ok('v1 analysis.json inputs == private file hashes', all(json.load(open(E/'results/analysis.json'))['inputs'][n]==sha((P/n).read_bytes()) for n in json.load(open(E/'results/analysis.json'))['inputs']))
ok('v1 launch.json freeze_sha256 == public v1 freeze.json', json.load(open(P/'launch.json'))['freeze_sha256']==sha((E/'sources/freeze.json').read_bytes()))
ok('v2 launch.json freeze_sha256 == public v2 freeze.json', json.load(open(P2/'launch.json'))['freeze_sha256']==sha((V/'sources/freeze.json').read_bytes()))
ok('v2 parent_freeze_sha256 == public v1 freeze.json', json.load(open(V/'sources/freeze.json'))['parent_freeze_sha256']==sha((E/'sources/freeze.json').read_bytes()))
ok('v1 launch wrapper_sha256 == private launch.py', json.load(open(P/'launch.json'))['wrapper_sha256']==sha((P/'launch.py').read_bytes()))
ok('v2 launch wrapper_sha256 == private v2 launch.py', json.load(open(P2/'launch.json'))['wrapper_sha256']==sha((P2/'launch.py').read_bytes()))
ok('provenance private_case_manifest_sha256 == cases.json', json.load(open(E/'sources/provenance.json'))['private_case_manifest_sha256']==sha((P/'cases.json').read_bytes()))
ok('provenance source hashes == private snapshots', all(sha((P/r['destination']).read_bytes())==r['sha256'] for r in json.load(open(E/'sources/provenance.json'))['sources']))
ok('target_checks source context hashes == cases.json context hashes', [r['context_sha256'] for r in json.load(open(E/'results/target_checks.json'))['source_replay']]==[c['context_sha256'] for c in json.load(open(P/'cases.json'))])
# targets context hashes vs artifacts
tg={t['artifact']:t for t in json.load(open(P2/'targets.json'))}
ok('targets context_sha256 == artifacts context_sha256 (valid rows)', all(tg[a['id']].get('context_sha256')==a['context_sha256'] for a in arts if 'context_sha256' in a))
ok('context_source hash recomputes', all(sha(a['context_source'].encode())==a['context_sha256'] for a in arts if 'context_source' in a))
ok('statement hash recomputes', all(sha(a['specification'].encode())==a['statement_sha256'] for a in arts))
# diagnostics public hashes vs private
d=json.load(open(E/'results/diagnostics.json')); props=json.load(open(P2/'diagnostic_proposals.json'))
ok('diagnostics proof_sha256 == private proposals', all(r['proof_sha256']==sha(props[r['artifact']].encode()) for r in d['rows']))
ok('diagnostics receipt_sha256 == private result.json (sort_keys)', all(r['receipt_sha256']==sha(json.dumps(json.load(open(P2/'diagnostics'/r['artifact']/'result.json')),sort_keys=True).encode()) for r in d['rows']))
ok('summary.json independent_counterexamples == diagnostics.json', json.load(open(E/'results/summary.json'))['independent_counterexamples']==d)
# reconstruct model inputs independently
cases={c['id']:c for c in json.load(open(P/'cases.json'))}
for a in arts:
    c=cases[a['task_id']]
    req=json.load(open(P2/'calls'/('generate_'+a['id'])/'request.json'))
    exp='PYTHON\n'+(P2/'cases'/a['task_id']/'Input.py').read_text()+'\nLEAN INTERFACE\n'+c['signature']
    ok(f'generation input {a["id"]} == PYTHON+Input.py+interface (no gold)', req['messages'][1]['content']==exp and 'GoldSpec' not in req['messages'][1]['content'])
    ok(f'generation system prompt {a["id"]} == committed prompt', req['messages'][0]['content']==(V/'prompts'/('generate_'+a['generator']+'.md')).read_text())
    for j in ['J0','J1']:
        req=json.load(open(P2/'calls'/f'forecast_{a["id"]}_{j}_0'/'request.json'))

        u=req['messages'][1]['content']
        ok(f'forecast input {a["id"]} {j} == reconstruction; no context/proof/outcome leakage', u==exp and 'import SpecOnly' not in u and 'Coverage' not in u and 'Nonvacuous' not in u and 'theorem' not in u and 'sorry' not in u and 'target' not in u.lower())
        ok(f'forecast system prompt {a["id"]} {j} == committed', req['messages'][0]['content']==(V/'prompts'/f'judge_{j}.md').read_text() and req['think']==False and req['options']['num_predict']==(256 if j=='J0' else 1024))
for ident in ['prove_T01_G0_0','prove_T01_G0_1','prove_T01_G1_0','prove_T01_G1_1','prove_T04_G0_0','prove_T04_G0_1']:
